subject: Rebaseline request: POC acceptance criteria + added checkout personalization use case
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Serrano <alex@brightcart.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Oct 2026 16:00:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap + proposed POC success criteria (next steps)

Hi Alex — great call today, thanks for walking through the BrightCart checkout flows. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the trial kicks off:

Summary of what we heard from BrightCart:
- Primary objective: reduce checkout abandonment and increase average order value via personalization.
- Must validate: latency at peak traffic, model quality for product recommendations, and safe fallback behavior under load.
- Security: SOC2 evidence and basic SSO for engineering access.

Proposed POC scope (initial):
- Ingest product catalog + user session snippets (anonymized) into a staging environment.
- Serve recommendations for 3 canonical checkout scenarios (guest checkout, logged-in returning user, promo flow).
- Evaluation: 3 quality slices (precision at top-3, CTR uplift, manual review for hallucination risk).

Deliverables & timeline (proposed):
- Week 0 (kickoff): environment access, data share checklist.
- Week 1–2: integration + sample traffic (Ben to assist).
- Week 3: evaluation run & acceptance metrics.
- Week 4: handover + recommendations.

I've attached a first-pass success criteria workbook (POC_Success_Criteria_v1.xlsx). Ask: can you confirm the three priority checkout flows and whether the procurement timelines you mentioned (channeling PO/contract) are still on track? If adding additional flows or use cases is required, we can rebaseline but will need to update the acceptance criteria and timeline.

Next steps (please):
1) Alex: confirm priority flows and procurement cadence.
2) BrightCart: confirm data access owner and expected date for sample extracts.
3) Ben/Marissa: I'll loop you both to confirm resource availability.

Thanks — looking forward to nailing the success criteria.

—
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.com
(415) 555-0198
From: Alex Serrano <alex@brightcart.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@brightcart.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + proposed POC success criteria (next steps)

Thanks Naomi — appreciate the clear recap. Two quick items from our side:

1) We want to add a small checkout personalization use case mid-trial: dynamic promo bundling on the checkout page (we believe this is high impact and overlaps with the recommendation surface). Will this require a full rebaseline?

2) Procurement: aiming to have PO routed by Oct 20 but SOW amendment may be needed if scope changes.

If rebaselining is required, can you sketch the minimal change set and timeline impact? Otherwise we should try to keep the initial integration focused and treat the bundling flow as an immediate follow-on sprint.

Alex Serrano
Head of Growth, BrightCart
alex@brightcart.com
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Serrano <alex@brightcart.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Oct 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + proposed POC success criteria (next steps)

Appreciate the fast reply, Alex. Short answer: yes, adding the promo-bundling flow changes the evaluation matrix but we can avoid a major timeline slip with a staged approach. Outline below — I attached an updated workbook (POC_Success_Criteria_v2.xlsx) with the changes highlighted.

Option A (staged — recommended):
- Keep core 3 checkout scenarios for Week 1–3 integration/eval.
- Add bundle promo flow as an additional evaluation slice in Week 3–4 with a lightweight integration (client-side call) so we can validate impact without full backend work.
- Acceptance: pass core metrics + a 2% relative uplift in promo conversion for the bundle slice.
- Timeline impact: +1 week for validation (new end date Week 5).

Option B (full inclusion):
- Expand initial integration to cover bundle flow end-to-end; requires backend hooks and additional mapping.
- Timeline impact: +2–3 weeks; requires updated SOW and procurement signoff before work starts.

We recommend Option A to keep momentum while allowing you to validate the high-impact bundle quickly.

Ben: can you confirm the technical feasibility of a client-side call for bundle recommendations and rough effort estimate?
Marissa: can you review the new acceptance thresholds in v2 and confirm telemetry we should capture for the bundle slice?

Alex — if you can confirm priority ranking (core / bundle) and procurement ETA, I'll lock the milestones and send a brief SOW amendment draft for signature.

—
Naomi
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Alex Serrano <alex@brightcart.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + proposed POC success criteria (next steps)

Looping in details from a CS/eval perspective. Short checklist and owners so we have clear accountability: 

Owners:
- Marissa (CS): overall POC success owner, will own metric sign-off and manual review samples.
- Ben (SE): integration owner, will own SDK/hook implementation and load test runs.
- Naomi (AE): commercial owner and SOW coordination.

Evaluation plan (concrete):
- Data/traffic: 48-hour sample test window for each flow, synthetic ramp to simulate peak (Ben).
- Metrics to capture: latency p95, top-3 precision, CTR uplift, conversion delta, false-positive rate (manual review).
- Acceptance gates: core flows must meet latency p95 <= 250ms and precision@3 >= 0.6; bundle slice target: +2% promo conversion uplift vs baseline.
- Governance: weekly 30-min checkpoint (Wednesdays) + final signoff meeting.

Dependencies:
- Sample extracts (anonymized) by Oct 12.
- Procurement/PO to enable staging capacity by Oct 20 (per Alex).

I'll update the POC_Success_Criteria_v2 workbook to include the telemetry fields and a simple rubric for manual review samples. Naomi — I'll need access to the shared Drive folder you referenced to drop the rubric and test templates.

Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
From: Alex Serrano <alex@brightcart.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@brightcart.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + proposed POC success criteria (next steps)

Thanks everyone — this looks good and aligned with our internal priorities. Quick additions from procurement/engineering:

- We accept Option A (staged). Priority ranking: 1) core checkout flows, 2) promo-bundling slice (client-side for POC).
- Procurement: we will aim to issue PO by Oct 20; please send the SOW amendment and one-page MOU for signature.
- Engineering asks: include an SSO test for Redwood engineers to access staging (we can provide SAML metadata next week).
- Attached: partially completed SOC2 questionnaire (SOC2_Questionnaire_BrightCart_partial.pdf) — please confirm what evidence you can share and expected turnaround for our audit lead.

Next steps (actionable):
1) Naomi: send SOW amendment + one-page MOU for signature.
2) Ben: confirm feasibility estimate for client-side bundle call and any sample code we can use.
3) Marissa: drop rubric and telemetry template in the Drive folder the week of Oct 12.

Once PO is in, we can lock the staging slot. Appreciate the quick coordination.

Alex Serrano
Head of Growth | BrightCart
alex@brightcart.com
